review: AI tells in the Dreamrules draft, second pass

before.title: Spice deck preparation
before.text: Use fifteen ordinary Spice Blow cards, five mine cards and six Shai-Hulud cards. Opening-deck questions are on p30.

after.title: Spice deck preparation
after.text: Use fifteen ordinary Spice Blow cards, five mine cards and six Shai-Hulud cards.

before.name: Trade information differently
before.text: Atreides may look at the top Nexus card instead of the top Spice card. Fremen gains Spice Blow Knowledge. Check for the Nexus before resolving any worm or mine.

before.name: Worms affect the board
before.text: Resolve Shai-Hulud against its affected territory and let Fremen use its riding powers. Track every drawn Shai-Hulud with a Shield Wall marker. A Thumper calls a riding worm but adds no Shield Wall marker.

after.name: Worms affect the board
after.text: Shai-Hulud eats spice and troops in its territory as usual, and Fremen can ride it. Track every drawn Shai-Hulud with a Shield Wall marker. A Thumper calls a riding worm but adds no Shield Wall marker.

before.name: Storm can contain a battle
before.text: Storm blocks ordinary movement, but does not itself stop battles or advisor flips in Dreamrules. Troops separated by the storm still cannot fight across it. The old FAQ banned battles even when both armies shared a protected sector under storm; Dreamrules permits them there.

after.name: Battles can happen under the storm
after.text: Storm blocks ordinary movement, but does not itself stop battles or advisor flips in Dreamrules. Troops separated by the storm still cannot fight across it. The old FAQ banned battles even when both armies shared a protected sector under storm; Dreamrules permits them there.

before.title: Replenishing a surviving mine
before.text: Top the mine up to its yield; don't add that amount to the spice left there. Replenishment timing is undecided, p30.

after.title: Replenishing a surviving mine
after.text: Top the mine up to its yield; don't add that amount to the spice left there.

before.name: Atreides can create another mine
before.text: Arrakis Fiefdom can place a three-spice mine in a sand territory without a Spice Blow marker. Its Carryall token pays when a mine sends troops to reserves. The faction chapter explains that Fate.

after.name: Atreides can create another mine
after.text: Atreides can create a mine with its Fate, see page 16.

before.name: Name the advantage
before.text: Use Karama at that advantage's window. It remains suppressed until the current phase ends, including later uses in that phase. Other advantages still work. A Bidding cancellation ends with Bidding; a Battle cancellation lasts across that faction's later battles.

after.name: Name the advantage
after.text: Use Karama at the time given for that advantage in the reference tables. It remains suppressed until the current phase ends, including later uses in that phase. Other advantages still work. A Bidding cancellation ends with Bidding; a Battle cancellation lasts across that faction's later battles.

before.name: Some windows close before plans are locked
before.text: Stop Sardaukar, Kwisatz Haderach, Spite or Retreat before plans are locked. Waiting for the leader to die or the Guild to announce Retreat is too late. The reference tables at the end list the windows.

after.name: Cancel before commitment
after.text: Stop Sardaukar, Kwisatz Haderach, Spite or Retreat before commitment. Waiting for the leader to die or the Guild to announce Retreat is too late.

before.name: Before plans
before.text: Resolve Supplies, Political Marriages and the final opportunity for an Ixian alliance card exchange. The Voice comes before Battle Prescience. Blackmail and Stone Burner follow Prescience. Then give everyone a chance to respond before plans are locked.

after.name: Before plans
after.text: First play any Supplies or Political Marriages you want to use. This is also the Ixians' last chance to swap a card with their ally. The Voice comes before Battle Prescience. Blackmail and Stone Burner follow Prescience. Then give everyone a chance to respond before commitment.

before.name: Lock the plans
before.text: Fremen reveals any cards it wants protected by Fanatical Tactics. Infiltrated factions lock their plans first so Bene Tleilax can look. Then everyone else locks theirs. Emperor and Ixian Fates cannot interrupt this step.

after.name: Commitment
after.text: Commitment is the step when both players lock their plans. Fremen reveals any cards it wants protected by Fanatical Tactics. Infiltrated factions commit their plans first so Bene Tleilax can look. Then everyone else commits theirs. Emperor and Ixian Fates cannot be played during commitment.

before.name: Traitor winners keep their played cards
before.text: GF9's FAQ lets a traitor winner discard played cards. Dreamrules requires the winner to keep them. The winning leader is available elsewhere afterward. A successful Break Conditioning result instead commits its leaders and allows the winner to discard.

after.name: Traitor winners keep their played cards
after.text: GF9's FAQ lets a traitor winner discard played cards. Dreamrules requires the winner to keep them. The winning leader is available elsewhere afterward. After Break Conditioning, both leaders stay committed to that territory. The winner may discard played cards.

before.name: One faction must hold all three
before.text: Holding all three standard tokens gives that faction one stronghold contribution for victory. Allies can't add their tokens together.

after.name: One faction must hold all three
after.text: Holding all three standard tokens counts as one stronghold for victory. Allies can't add their tokens together.

before.name: Start after turn ten's Nexus
before.text: If nobody has won when turn ten's Nexus ends, enter sudden death. There is no automatic win for Fremen or Guild. This also applies when Fremen is absent.

after.name: Start after turn ten's Nexus
after.text: If nobody has won when turn ten's Nexus ends, enter sudden death. There is no automatic win for Fremen or Guild.

before.name: Watch Nexus instead of Spice
before.text: Replace Spice Prescience with Nexus Prescience. You may inspect the top Nexus card. Fremen now has the upcoming Spice information. Your auction inspection remains.

after.name: Watch Nexus instead of Spice
after.text: Nexus Prescience lets you inspect the top Nexus card. Your auction inspection remains.

before.title: Carryall income and victory
before.text: Carryall is outside the seven-token pool. Whether it counts toward token income and victory is undecided, p30.

after.title: Carryall income and victory
after.text: Carryall is outside the seven-token pool.

before.name: Spite has exceptions
before.text: A dead Cheap Hero, a traitor result or successful Break Conditioning does not trigger Spite. Cheap Heroes cannot be swapped. A Fremen card protected by Fanatical Tactics may only be replaced with a card of the same color. Supplies cards are an open question, p30.

after.name: Spite has exceptions
after.text: A dead Cheap Hero, a traitor result or successful Break Conditioning does not trigger Spite. Cheap Heroes cannot be swapped. A Fremen card protected by Fanatical Tactics may only be replaced with a card of the same color.

before.name: Fate reveals a whole plan
before.text: After Prescience, before plans are locked, play Blackmail to make your own or your ally's opponent reveal its whole battle plan early. This replaces the old special Karama hand exchange.

after.name: Fate reveals a whole plan
after.text: After Prescience, before commitment, play Blackmail to make your own or your ally's opponent reveal its whole battle plan early. This replaces the old special Karama hand exchange.

before.name: Prison Planet is paid revival
before.text: Your Fate revives up to five troops of any kind and one leader at their normal prices. You may revive pieces for other factions. These revivals bypass the ordinary leader and starred-troop limits, and Bene Tleilax earns no income from them. Use it at any time except while battle plans are being locked.

after.name: Prison Planet is paid revival
after.text: Your Fate revives up to five troops of any kind and one leader at their normal prices. You may revive pieces for other factions. These revivals bypass the ordinary leader and starred-troop limits, and Bene Tleilax earns no income from them. Use it at any time except during commitment.

before.title: Retreat exceptions
before.text: A resolved traitor or Break Conditioning prevents Retreat. The order of those choices and the opponent's losses and rewards are undecided, p30.

after.title: Retreat exceptions
after.text: A resolved traitor or Break Conditioning prevents Retreat.

before.name: Inspect the Spice draws
before.text: Spice Blow Knowledge transfers upcoming Spice information from Atreides to you. Which cards you may inspect depends on the unresolved draw-pile setup, p30.

after.name: Inspect the Spice draws
after.text: Spice Blow Knowledge lets you inspect upcoming Spice cards. This replaces Atreides' Spice Prescience.

before.name: Reveal cards to protect them
before.text: As plans are locked, Fanatical Tactics lets you publicly reveal a weapon, a defense or both from your battle plan. Keep the revealed cards even after an ordinary defeat. A traitor call against your leader or a Lasgun-Shield explosion still loses them.

after.name: Reveal cards to protect them
after.text: During commitment, Fanatical Tactics lets you publicly reveal a weapon, a defense or both from your battle plan. Keep the revealed cards even after an ordinary defeat. A traitor call against your leader or a Lasgun-Shield explosion still loses them.

before.name: Spite must keep the color
before.text: Harkonnen may replace a protected card only with a card of the same color. Protected Supplies cards at phase end are an open question, p30.

after.name: Spite must keep the color
after.text: Harkonnen may replace a protected card only with a card of the same color.

before.name: Turn advisors into fighters at the phase start
before.text: At the start of Shipment and Movement, you may turn advisor groups into fighters. A group alone turns automatically. After that window, advisors stay advisors even if every other faction in their territory leaves or dies.

after.name: Turn advisors into fighters at the phase start
after.text: At the start of Shipment and Movement, you may turn advisor groups into fighters. A group alone turns automatically. For the rest of the phase, advisors stay advisors even if every other faction in their territory leaves or dies.

before.name: Fate extends Voice to nearby battles
before.text: At the Voice window, play Political Marriages. For the rest of that turn, use Voice on one side in any battle where you have advisors. Karama cannot stop this Voice.

after.name: Fate extends Voice to nearby battles
after.text: Before The Voice, play Political Marriages. For the rest of that turn, use Voice on one side in any battle where you have advisors. Karama cannot stop this Voice.

before.name: Deal restrictions
before.text: Outside Mentat you cannot give or receive bribes. You cannot make most binding deals or bindingly show cards. You may buy binding information about auction cards and, during Mentat, promise to end a named Face Dancer Infiltration. Your ally may still share cards with you as the alliance rules allow.

after.name: Deal restrictions
after.text: Outside Mentat you cannot give or receive bribes. Most of your deals aren't binding, and you can't make a binding promise to show cards. You may buy binding information about auction cards and, during Mentat, promise to end a named Face Dancer Infiltration. Your ally can still show you cards.

before.name: Fate removes support in one territory
before.text: Before plans are locked, play Stone Burner. For the rest of Battle, troops in that territory cannot use spice support, including Fremen.

after.name: Fate removes support in one territory
after.text: Before commitment, play Stone Burner. For the rest of Battle, troops in that territory cannot use spice support, including Fremen.

before.title: Other player counts
before.text: The starting deal for games with fewer or more than six players is undecided, p30.

after.text: Open question, see page 30.

before.name: Inspect the infiltrated faction
before.text: While the revived leader lives and you hold the Face Dancer card, inspect that faction's spice and Treachery Cards at any time. Inspect its battle plan as plans are locked. You may advise its opponent. When two infiltrated factions fight, let at most one change its plan after your inspection.

after.name: Inspect the infiltrated faction
after.text: While the revived leader lives and you hold the Face Dancer card, inspect that faction's spice and Treachery Cards at any time. Inspect its battle plan during commitment. You may advise its opponent. When two infiltrated factions fight, let at most one change its plan after your inspection.

before.title: Storm window
before.text: Infiltration's exact timing during Storm is undecided, p30.

after.text: Open question, see page 30.

before.name: Exchange a card with your ally
before.text: Once per turn, you and your ally may swap or transfer one Treachery Card. Use the pre-plan window during battle. This replaces the GF9 benefit that let your ally discard a newly bought card and draw a replacement. It is separate from your auction-card exchange.

after.name: Exchange a card with your ally
after.text: Once per turn, you and your ally may swap or transfer one Treachery Card. In battle, exchange cards before plans are made. This replaces the GF9 benefit that let your ally discard a newly bought card and draw a replacement. It is separate from your auction-card exchange.

before.name: Fate blocks one special card for the turn
before.text: Play Defect before a special card is used or in response to the attempted play. Return an interrupted card to its owner. It cannot be used again that turn. To stop Mercenaries or a special weapon or defense, act before plans are made. Defect cannot interrupt the step when plans are locked.

after.name: Fate blocks one special card for the turn
after.text: Play Defect before a special card is used or in response to the attempted play. Return an interrupted card to its owner. It cannot be used again that turn. To stop Mercenaries or a special weapon or defense, act before plans are made. Defect cannot be played during commitment.

before.name: Political Marriages
before.text: Karama cannot stop the Voice granted by this Fate. Prediction is also outside the listed cancellation effects.

after.name: Political Marriages
after.text: Karama cannot stop the Voice granted by this Fate. It can't stop Prediction either.

before.name: Six Shai-Hulud cards
before.text: Use six Shai-Hulud cards. How to shuffle them into the opening deck is still open.

before.name: Insert Nexus after Storm
before.text: The order is Storm, Nexus, Spice Blow, CHOAM Charity, Bidding, Revival, Shipment and Movement, Battle, Spice Collection, Mentat. A drawn worm no longer creates an alliance window.

after.name: Insert Nexus after Storm
after.text: The order is Storm, Nexus, Spice Blow, CHOAM Charity, Bidding, Revival, Shipment and Movement, Battle, Spice Collection, Mentat. A drawn worm no longer lets players change alliances.

before.title: Stop Mercenaries before planning
before.text: Play Defect naming Mercenaries before battle plans are made. Opponents cannot include it later that turn. Waiting until an opposing plan reveals Mercenaries misses the window.

after.title: Stop Mercenaries before planning
after.text: Play Defect naming Mercenaries before battle plans are made. Opponents cannot include it later that turn. After Mercenaries is revealed, Defect is too late.

ruleChecks: Quickstart v0.8 calls step 3 Commitment of Battle Plans. The guide defines commitment on page 8 and uses it for timing.
The Bene Tleilax sheet forbids binding deals and binding disclosure, with exceptions for auction information and ending a Face Dancer Infiltration. The exceptions remain explicit.
Supplies and Political Marriages remain optional card plays in the battle sequence.
Leader commitment remains distinct from locking battle plans and from Truthtrance promises.
